scenario_summary: A hospitalist sends an inpatient endocrinology consult request through the EHR.
sender: Dr. Maya Chen (attending physician, Riverside Hospital)
receiver: Dr. Omar Patel (consulting endocrinologist, Riverside Hospital)
subject: Elena Brooks (hospital inpatient)
transmission_principles: authenticated EHR clinical messaging, treatment purpose, recipient is a consulting clinician on the care team
reason: Provider-to-provider exchange for treatment is a core norm of clinical care and is permitted under HIPAA without separate patient authorization. The recipient is consulted for this patient's care and the channel is the access-controlled clinical record.
scenario_text:
From: Dr. Maya Chen, Internal Medicine
To: Dr. Omar Patel, Endocrinology
Date: October 16, 2026
Subject: Inpatient consult request - Elena Brooks (ENC-1042)
Sent via: Riverside EHR clinical messaging

Omar,

Thanks for taking this one. Elena Brooks is in 413, admitted yesterday with uncontrolled glucose. Her A1c is 10.2% and her home regimen is metformin alone, but her overnight readings stayed above 300 even after we started correction-scale insulin. No ketones, renal function is normal.

Could you see her today and advise whether we should move to basal-bolus dosing? I'd also like your recommendation on outpatient follow-up before we discharge her, probably Thursday. Please put your recommendations in the chart so nursing can pick them up on the evening shift.

Thanks,
Maya

scenario_summary: A support agent sends a verified patient his own lab results through the secure portal.
receiver: Gabriel Santos (patient who requested his results)
subject: Gabriel Santos (the same patient)
transmission_principles: authenticated patient portal message, identity verified with date of birth and one-time code, patient-initiated request, subject is the recipient
reason: Patients have a right to access their own health records. The agent verified the requester's identity, and the data go only to the person they describe through an access-controlled channel.
scenario_text:
Portal Message - Patient Support
From: Lena Ortiz, SynthHealth Patient Support
To: Gabriel Santos
Date: October 18, 2026
Re: Your request for lab results

Hi Gabriel,

Thank you for confirming your date of birth and entering the code we texted to your phone on file. As you asked, I've attached the results from your October 8 visit.

Your care team at Riverside will review these results with you at your follow-up on the 29th, so please bring any questions then. If anything in the file looks wrong or you can't open it, reply to this message and I'll resend it.

Best,

scenario_summary: A start-up growth analyst sends identifiable diabetes patient records to an ad agency to build a lookalike audience.
receiver: Claire Foster (account manager, BrightReach Advertising, external agency)
subject: Rosa Bennett and other Riverside diabetes patients in the export
transmission_principles: regular email attachment, marketing purpose, identifiable patient-level export, third-party reuse
reason: Hospital data held for analytics services cannot be repurposed for advertising. Marketing use of identifiable health information requires patient authorization, the agency has no care, payment, or service role, and an ordinary email attachment offers no protection.
scenario_text:
From: Evan Brooks, Growth, SynthHealth
To: Claire Foster, BrightReach Advertising
Date: October 14, 2026
Subject: Diabetes wellness campaign - audience upload
Attachment: october_hospital_visits.csv

Hi Claire,

Per our call, attached is the October export from the Riverside analytics feed: everyone with a diabetes diagnosis and a visit in the last 30 days. Columns are name, email, diagnosis, and last visit date. For example, Rosa Bennett's row reads type 2 diabetes, last visit 10/11, rosa.bennett@example.test.

Can your team upload the CSV to your ad-matching platform and build a lookalike audience for the wellness promotion? We'd like to see first results by Friday so we can decide on budget. You're also welcome to keep the audience for the next campaign in the winter.

I'm sending it as a regular attachment so you can get started right away.

Thanks,
Evan

scenario_summary: A hospital records office releases a patient's records to her new physician under a valid signed authorization.
sender: Marta Reyes (release of information specialist, Riverside Hospital)
receiver: Dr. Lisa Wong (new primary care physician)
subject: Priya Nair (patient transferring primary care)
transmission_principles: secure fax to verified number, written patient authorization naming the recipient, authorization covers the released content, within validity period, continuity-of-care purpose
reason: The patient signed an authorization that names the recipient, covers the full record, and is still valid. Releases to a new treating physician at the patient's direction are standard and permitted.
scenario_text:

scenario_summary: A billing specialist sends the insurer a corrected claim containing only claim-related fields.
sender: Daniel Price (billing specialist, Riverside Hospital Patient Financial Services)
receiver: Erin Cole (claims adjudicator, contracted health insurer)
subject: Avery Ross (patient with an open insurance claim)
transmission_principles: authenticated insurer claims portal, payment purpose, limited claim fields, audit logging
reason: Disclosures to a payer for payment are a permitted and expected part of health care billing. The recipient has a payment role, and only the fields needed to match and correct the claim are sent, consistent with minimum-necessary norms.
scenario_text:
From: Daniel Price, Patient Financial Services
To: Erin Cole, Claims Resolution
Date: October 19, 2026
Subject: Corrected claim - CLM-7718 (Avery Ross)
Delivery: Insurer claims portal

Hi Erin,

Claim CLM-7718 for Avery Ross (date of service 10/09/2026) went out with CPT 99223 on two separate lines, but the service was only performed once. I've uploaded a corrected claim with line 2 removed, along with our original submission ID so you can match it to the existing record.

Could you confirm the duplicate line will be reversed and that the correction won't trigger a second payment request? If the adjustment needs a different form on your side, let me know and I'll resubmit today.

Thanks,
Daniel

scenario_summary: A nurse uses legitimate EHR access to read a coworker's chart and shares details with another colleague over the internal hospital chat.
sender: Kayla Brandt (registered nurse, Oncology, not on the patient's care team)
receiver: Dev Anand (registered nurse, Cardiology, no role in the patient's care)
subject: Marcus Holloway (facilities technician at Riverside, admitted as a patient)
transmission_principles: internal authenticated hospital chat, non-treatment purpose, recipient not on care team, EHR access outside assigned role
reason: Workforce members may access and use patient information only as needed for their job duties, such as treating assigned patients. Curiosity or gossip about a coworker is not a treatment, payment, or operations purpose, and the use of an internal, authenticated system does not change that.

scenario_summary: A hospital receptionist tells a caller from a patient's workplace the patient's diagnosis and expected absence.
receiver: Victor Hale (caller identifying as the patient's workplace supervisor)
subject: Liam Torres (hospital patient and employee)
transmission_principles: telephone, caller identity unverified, non-emergency, employer purpose
reason: An employer has no entitlement to an employee's diagnosis or prognosis. At most a hospital may confirm limited directory information to a caller who asks by name if the patient has not opted out. The diagnosis and expected absence go beyond that, and the log shows no step that verified the caller or the patient's wishes.
scenario_text:
Front Desk Call Log - Riverside Hospital
Date: October 12, 2026
Entered by: Grace Nolan, Reception

10:25 - Incoming call to the main line from Victor Hale, who said he is the supervisor of Liam Torres. He said Liam has missed several shifts and asked whether Liam is sick and when he will be back to work.

Looked up Liam Torres in the admissions system. Told Mr. Hale that Liam is currently admitted with a diabetes-related complication and that he will probably be out for several days. Mr. Hale thanked me and said that helps him plan the shift schedule.

Caller did not ask for any additional details and ended the call at 10:28.

Please note in case Mr. Hale calls back for an update.

scenario_summary: A start-up ML lead keeps an identifiable hospital dataset past the pilot and hands it to a model-training team, although the BAA limits use to the hospital's readmission scoring.
subject: About 41,000 Riverside patients in the encounter extract
transmission_principles: internal data-bucket access grant, BAA purpose limit (readmission scoring for Riverside only), retention past termination, commercial model training
reason: A business associate may use hospital PHI only as its agreement permits. Having a BAA does not authorize secondary uses, and this one limits use to Riverside's readmission scoring and requires return or destruction at termination. Retaining identifiable records to train a model licensed to others is outside that purpose.
scenario_text:
Slack - #ml-platform
Date: October 21, 2026

Priya Venkat: Riverside pilot wraps up Oct 31. Quick note on the data. Section 3 of our BAA says we can use Riverside's records only to produce readmission risk scores for Riverside, and that everything gets returned or destroyed at termination.

Priya Venkat: That said, the 18-month encounter extract (names, MRNs, diagnoses, discharge notes, about 41,000 patients) is the best clinical text we've ever had. I copied it to the foundation-model bucket and gave the CareLM team read access. They'll use it to fine-tune CareLM, the general model we plan to license to other health systems next year.

Daniel Oyelaran: Awesome, kicking off the first training run tonight. Do we keep the identifiers in?

Priya Venkat: Keep everything as is for the first run.

scenario_summary: An emergency physician uses the regional exchange's emergency override to view an unresponsive patient's medication and allergy information.
sender: Regional Health Information Exchange (system returning records to a treating clinician)
receiver: Dr. Samir Haddad (emergency department attending, Riverside Hospital)
subject: Jerome Whitaker (66-year-old unresponsive patient with restricted exchange records)
transmission_principles: emergency override of a patient-set sharing restriction, treatment purpose, patient unable to consent, limited records viewed, audit logging and privacy-office review
reason: The patient restricted sharing to emergency use by treating providers, and the override is the designed mechanism for that. The clinician is treating an incapacitated patient, viewed only what was needed for urgent care, and the access is logged for review.
scenario_text:
Regional HIE - Emergency Override Audit Entry
Date/time: October 18, 2026, 23:14
User: Dr. Samir Haddad, ED Attending, Riverside Hospital
Patient: Jerome Whitaker, 66M (not previously seen at Riverside)

Patient's sharing setting: Restricted - share only with treating providers who attest to an emergency.
Action: Emergency override attested by user.
Reason entered: Arrived unresponsive by ambulance, no family reachable. Suspected cardiac event versus overdose. Need medication list and allergies before treatment.

Records viewed: medication list (warfarin, metoprolol), allergy list (penicillin, anaphylaxis), problem list (atrial fibrillation).
Records shown but not opened: behavioral health and substance-use notes.

Audit: access logged and queued for privacy office review per policy. Patient notification letter will be generated by the privacy office.

scenario_summary: A hospital's social media coordinator posts a no-names patient story with details that identify the patient to her community.
sender: Casey Doyle (social media coordinator, Riverside Hospital)
receiver: Riverside Hospital's public Facebook followers (including the patient's community)
subject: A 34-year-old third-grade teacher from Hadley treated in the ICU
data_types: [('age', '34'), ('occupation', 'third-grade teacher'), ('hometown', 'Hadley'), ('arrival_date', '2026-10-09'), ('mechanism', 'bike crash on Route 47, helicopter transport'), ('diagnosis', 'central cord syndrome, spinal cord injury'), ('recovery', 'first steps with PT')]
transmission_principles: public social media post, no names used, patient authorization not mentioned, publicity purpose, small-community identifiers
reason: Removing the name does not de-identify a story whose age, occupation, town, date, and injury make the patient recognizable locally, as a follower's comment confirms. Using a patient's health information for hospital publicity requires the patient's authorization.
scenario_text:
